intelligence_center.summary: June Brand Listening is verified for June 1-30, 2026. Talkwalker shows 73 results, 318 engagements, 60 unique authors, and 9 unique sites. Raw sentiment is mixed, with 39.7% negative, 37.0% positive, and 23.3% neutral, but manual review shows the negative bucket is dominated by Ebola/Marburg outbreak context rather than direct criticism of Sabin.

decision_rules: Treat June Talkwalker volume, engagement, author, site, media mix, and audience widgets as verified June metrics.
Do not use the raw 39.7% negative share as a public reputation score without the manual caveat.
Escalate only if negative labels include direct criticism, misinformation, confusion about Sabin's role, or credible high-reach authors targeting Sabin.
Keep owned Sabin posts, partner amplification, third-party outbreak news, and genuine criticism separate before reporting reputation health.
weekly_questions: Did any negative result directly criticize Sabin, or was it negative context around outbreak severity?
Which repeated outbreak terms are useful early-warning signals for Comms?
Which partner or owned content can clarify Sabin's role in Marburg/Ebola vaccine research without amplifying fear-based framing?
Which June themes from Talkwalker line up with Hootsuite engagement and GA4 audience behavior?
next_actions: Use the June Brand Listening metrics as the monthly listening baseline.
Add a sentiment caveat in any executive readout: June negativity is issue-context driven, not observed reputational criticism.
Monitor CIDRAP-style outbreak amplification separately from brand sentiment.
For future months, export negative results directly from Talkwalker and archive the raw CSV with the dashboard source package.
intelligence_center.monthly_export_status: Authenticated Brand Listening app reviewed for June 1-30, 2026. Raw CSV export was generated in Talkwalker but could not be downloaded through Chrome; expanded in-app review is attached as the source basis.

strengths: The dashboard now has verified June Talkwalker source coverage instead of stale shared-report placeholders.
Conversation volume is small enough for meaningful manual review: 73 total results and 29 negative-labeled results.
Owned Sabin channels remain prominent in the influencer view, with Sabin LinkedIn producing the strongest author engagement signal.
LinkedIn is the largest media-type share at 30.1%, followed by X at 20.5% and Bluesky at 13.7%.
vulnerabilities: Raw listening volume, engagement, author breadth, and site breadth were all down sharply against the prior period.
Talkwalker labels 39.7% of the conversation negative, but that number is easy to misread without manual context.

Negative labels are concentrated around outbreak severity, fatality, security, and vaccine availability language, so the dashboard should avoid presenting the raw split as public disapproval of Sabin.
The generated CSV export could not be retained locally, so the June negative-review audit relies on the expanded in-app view rather than a durable row-level file.
opportunities: Use the negative review as an internal method improvement: sentiment needs driver review before it becomes a reputation claim.
Separate issue-monitoring from brand sentiment in monthly reporting, especially for Ebola, Marburg, outbreak response, and vaccine-pipeline conversations.
Use Sabin's owned Marburg and outbreak-response content to clarify expertise while avoiding unnecessarily alarming framing.
Archive future Talkwalker CSV exports immediately so result-level classification can be reproduced.
content_ideas: Create a short internal note explaining why outbreak-related negative sentiment is not the same as anti-Sabin sentiment.
Prepare a plain-language explanation of Sabin's role in filovirus vaccine research that can be used when outbreak coverage spikes.
Use LinkedIn as the primary amplification channel for research, awards, and partner-credibility stories because it held the largest share of June conversation.
Pair future outbreak posts with clear context, source citations, and next-step links so negative public-health language does not become ambiguous brand sentiment.
discussion_points: The June Talkwalker problem was not missing data; it was interpretability. The live app had the right date range, but raw sentiment needed human review.
The correct leadership takeaway is: monitor outbreak-context negativity, but do not report it as evidence of reputational damage without direct criticism.
Negative-result curation should become a recurring monthly step for Talkwalker before sentiment appears in executive or board materials.
insights.summary: June Brand Listening is now verified from the authenticated Talkwalker app for June 1-30, 2026. The month shows 73 results, 318 engagements, 60 unique authors, and 9 unique sites. Raw sentiment is 37.0% positive, 23.3% neutral, and 39.7% negative, but manual review shows the negative set is dominated by Ebola/Marburg outbreak context, CIDRAP repost amplification, and vaccine-pipeline references rather than direct criticism of Sabin. Report the raw sentiment only with that caveat.
